original_question: Can one prove an average-type lower bound, analogous to Open Problem 2, for the discrepancy of digital nets generated by rational functions over finite fields?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Open Problem 3: “Give an average-type lower bound (in the style as stated in the Open Problem 2) for the discrepancy of digital nets generated by rational functions over finite fields.”
correct_elements: The draft is aimed at the correct target almost verbatim. It correctly asks for an average-type lower bound, explicitly ties the problem to Open Problem 2, and identifies the right class of objects: digital nets generated by rational functions over finite fields.
missing_details: The paper’s surrounding context fixes a dimension s and a prime base q; these parameters should be stated explicitly.

The averaging set is not specified. In the nearby setup, one chooses f in F_q[x] with deg(f)=m and polynomials g_1,...,g_s in F_q[x] with deg(g_i)<m; an average-type statement should count admissible tuples (f,g_1,...,g_s) of this form.

The point set itself should be defined: it is the q^m-point set in [0,1)^s obtained from the rational functions g_i/f via the polynomial n(x) attached to the q-adic digits of n and truncation of the Laurent expansion to the first m base-q digits.

The draft does not spell out what “average-type” means quantitatively. In the style of Open Problem 2 / Theorem 2.8, it should be a positive-proportion counting statement, e.g. at least c_{q,s}|A_m| admissible tuples for a suitable parameter set A_m.

The expected size of the lower bound is implicit. From the nearby upper bounds (Theorem 2.9 and the comparison with Open Problem 2), the intended scale is of order (log N)^(s-1) log log N / N with N=q^m.
The quantifier over m is left implicit. A stand-alone question should say whether the positive-proportion lower bound is sought for every sufficiently large m or only for infinitely many m.
The paper says “discrepancy,” not a different discrepancy notion; a stand-alone rewrite should preserve that terminology unless a change is explicitly justified from the paper.
refined_question: Fix s >= 1 and a prime q. For each m >= 1, let A_m be the set of all tuples (f,g_1,...,g_s) with f,g_i in F_q[x], deg(f)=m, and deg(g_i)<m for 1 <= i <= s, and let P(f,g_1,...,g_s) subset [0,1)^s be the q^m-point set obtained in Section 2 from the rational functions g_i/f, namely from the points (phi_m(n(x)g_1(x)/f(x)),...,phi_m(n(x)g_s(x)/f(x))) as n runs from 0 to q^m-1, where n(x) is the polynomial attached to the q-adic digits of n and phi_m truncates the Laurent expansion to its first m base-q digits. Does there exist a constant c_{q,s}>0 such that, for every sufficiently large m, at least c_{q,s}|A_m| admissible tuples (f,g_1,...,g_s) yield a net P(f,g_1,...,g_s) whose discrepancy satisfies D_{q^m}(P(f,g_1,...,g_s)) >= c_{q,s}(log(q^m))^(s-1) log log(q^m) / q^m? In other words, can one prove for this rational-function class the same kind of average-type lower bound that Open Problem 2 asks for digital nets over F_q?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official wording, so the target is clearly Open Problem 3 in Section 2. To make it stand-alone, however, one has to import the nearby definitions and scale from the surrounding discussion: the paragraph introducing digital nets generated by rational functions over finite fields supplies the ambient field and the rational-function construction, while Theorem 2.9 and Open Problem 2 indicate the intended discrepancy order and the counting/proportion-style meaning of “average-type.” No explicit paper-proved equivalent reformulation of Open Problem 3 is given, so no alternate version should be added.
